newsitem.title: USA: Marco dissipates off Cuban coast.
newsitem.headline: Marco dissipates off Cuban coast.

text.p: Former Hurricane Marco faded in the Caribbean Sea on Tuesday after a week of erratic wandering between Central America and Cuba, the National Hurricane Center said.

At 4 p.m. EST (2100 GMT), the late-season storm was centered at latitude 19.3 north, longitude 85.1 west, about 175 miles (280 km) south of Cabo San Antonio on the western tip of Cuba and moving southwest near 8 mph (13 kph).
The storm had maximum sustained winds of 30 mph (48 kph), and was expected to be absorbed by a nearby cold front, hurricane center forecasters said.
The hurricane center said it would not issue any more advisories on the storm unless it regenerated.
On Monday the storm unexpectedly reached tropical storm strength again after waxing and waning in the Caribbean Sea for the past week. Two deaths in Nicaragua were blamed on Marco's torrential rain.
The weakening of the storm was good news for Cuba, which was pounded by Hurricane Lili on Oct. 17 and 18, destroying about 5,000 homes and damaging crops, power lines and communications.
